name: r8-m09
statement: Think-SFT copies a teacher ending that puts the final value on the line after an 'Answer:' marker, which grader v3's last-marker rule reads as a blank answer, at a fixed rate per finished answer whatever the problem's difficulty; adding the RL-Math delta (Think-SFT + a(RL - base), a >= 2) replaces that ending with RL's single \boxed{} line, so the hybrid gains about 4 per 500 on MATH-500 (about 2 per 328 on hard328) from grading alone, on top of the finishing gain it gets from fewer cap hits.
scope: Covers allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Think-SFT with the cue and its hybrids Think-SFT + a(RL-Math - base), scored by grader v3 at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 on MATH-500, hard328 and fresh2026 (any cap). It explains a fixed per-answer grading loss and its removal by the RL delta. It does not explain Think-SFT's reasoning lead on long hard answers, its cap hits, or the hybrid's finishing gain on hard328, which is mostly real (cap hits 94.5 -> 54). It says nothing about the base, RL, or base + a(RL - base), whose layouts v3 reads (result-0018d3, result-dba8ee). If grader v4 already reads the next line after an empty 'Answer:', then v4 numbers carry no such loss.

imports.finding: Rule-based math verifiers keep >99 % precision but miss correct answers written in other formats, and recall is lower for long-CoT generators (R1-Distill ~0.92).
imports.how: Supplies the general mechanism: a rule grader's recall depends on the generator's answer layout. Think-SFT is a long-CoT imitator of teacher traces, so its recall under v3 falls below that of RL and the base, while precision stays intact.

imports.finding: Correctness-reward RL drives generations to one output format within the first epoch and suppresses the others.
imports.how: Explains why the RL-Math delta carries a format component (a single boxed ending) that moves to another host when added. That component removes the teacher layout from the hybrid.

explains.quote: 16 of its 74 finished wrong answers end in a line equal to the gold
explains.how: Those 16 are teacher-layout endings whose value sits on the line after 'Answer:', which v3 reads as blank; RL's boxed endings give 0 of 131.
Of the hybrid's 5-10 point lead over Think-SFT's single samples (457-462), about 4 points come from the boxed ending removing the v3 layout miss rather than from new right answers.

explains.quote: levels 1-2 Think-SFT 10 wrong vs RL 2.0 and base 8.5
explains.how: A layout miss that occurs at a fixed rate per finished answer shows up as excess errors where real errors are rare, which is the easy levels.

explains.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
explains.how: Adding the RL delta moves the host to RL's answer format, the step this mechanism needs for the hybrid's ending to switch.

explains.quote: finished answers with no boxed answer fall 22 -> 1
explains.how: The RL difference carries a boxed-ending component that rewrites the host's final line, so the same component, added to Think-SFT, ends its unboxed teacher layout.

conflicts.quote: Clean 322 and grader v4 move no share by more than 3.5 points.
conflicts.how: If v4's extra rules read the line after an empty 'Answer:', this caps Think-SFT's hard328 layout loss at about 1.5 problems per sample, below the about 2 the mechanism implies. Which rules v4 has is not stated.

A Think-SFT format theory (r7-m09) gained nothing over readers with no theory. That theory placed the miss on easy, non-integer problems; this one must hold at every difficulty and is refuted if it does not.
Repairing the grading should raise right-of-finished by about 1 point. The large fall shows that finishing hard problems dominates on hard328, so the grading part is not visible in these totals.

rival: Hedged correction: on problems it is unsure of, Think-SFT writes a wrong value on the 'Answer:' line and then appends a second, right candidate on the next line. v3 correctly grades the marked value, and the hybrid's gains are all real reliability. Two observations separate the accounts. (1) The extraction v3 took for these rows: the layout account says blank (or only markup), while the hedge account says a non-blank wrong value. (2) Difficulty: the layout account gives the same rate per finished answer at every cued-base solve count, while the hedge account puts most such rows on hard problems (base k <= 1).

predictions.experiment: Phenomenon on hard328 (no item reports it): among Think-SFT cue's finished, v3-wrong hard328 answers (4 single-sample full-text jobs), the share whose first non-empty text after the last 'Answer:' (or, with no marker, the last non-empty line) agrees with gold.
predictions.recipe: Files: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1115-000503-1e5f/answers.jsonl, -000525-ea4e, -014823-ef56, -014833-1daa (fetch with modal volume get as in inventory.md); agreement function rln4_lib.agree from studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py. In each file keep the first row per problem_index in file order. Finished = cap_hit not true and finish_reason != 'length'. Wrong = score_v3 != 1 (null or missing counts as wrong). Candidate C per row: if text contains the case-sensitive substring 'Answer:', let s = text after its last occurrence and C = the first element of s.split('\n') whose strip() is non-empty (this may be the rest of the marker line itself); if 'Answer:' is absent, C = the last element of text.split('\n') whose strip() is non-empty; if there is no such element, C = ''. Clean C: strip whitespace; remove every '$' and '*'; remove leading '\[' or '\(' and trailing '\]' or '\)'; strip a trailing '.'; if C contains '\boxed{', replace C by the brace-balanced content of its last \boxed{...}. The row counts if C is non-empty and rln4_lib.agree(C, gold) is true. Statistic = counted rows / finished wrong rows, pooled over the 4 files. Cap hits are excluded; missing rows add nothing.
predictions.refuted_by: measured below 0.025, or fewer than 40 finished wrong rows

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test, difficulty: the rate of layout misses per finished Think-SFT answer on problems the cued base solves at most 1 of 4 times, minus the rate on problems it solves 4 of 4. This mechanism (a fixed per-answer layout habit) predicts about 0.000. The hedged-correction rival (a second candidate added when unsure) puts these rows on hard problems and predicts about +0.015 or more. The r7-m09 easy-format account predicts a clearly negative value.
predictions.recipe: Files: the 4 Think-SFT hard328 full-text files of the first recipe, plus the 4 Think-SFT MATH-500 full-text files iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1115-000512-ee03/answers.jsonl, -014843-85d9, -000607-0e92, -000621-1d7e; studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl. In each Think-SFT file keep the first row per problem_index. Finished, wrong, candidate C, cleaning and 'layout row' (finished, wrong, C non-empty and rln4_lib.agree(C, gold) true) exactly as in the first recipe. k per problem and set: in the matching base rows.jsonl, for each sample s in {0,1,2,3} take the first row in file order with that problem_index, attempt == 0 and sample == s; k = number with score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit not true (a missing row is not right). Easy = k == 4; Hard = k <= 1; other k are dropped. Problems are matched within a set only (MATH-500 Think-SFT rows with MATH-500 base rows, hard328 with hard328). Pool all 8 files: rate_X = layout rows in stratum X / finished rows in stratum X. Statistic = rate_Hard - rate_Easy. Cap hits are excluded from both numerator and denominator; problems with no base rows are dropped.
predictions.unit: difference of fractions of finished answers
predictions.refuted_by: measured above 0.014 or below -0.010, or either stratum has fewer than 150 finished rows

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test, what v3 read: among Think-SFT layout rows (finished, v3-wrong, gold-agreeing candidate after the last 'Answer:'), the share whose stored extracted_v3 is blank or markup only. The line-break mechanism says v3 read an empty marker line and predicts a large share. The hedged-correction rival says the 'Answer:' line held a real wrong value and predicts a small share (below 0.3).
predictions.recipe: Files: the 8 Think-SFT full-text files of the second recipe (4 hard328, 4 MATH-500). First row per problem_index per file. Layout rows exactly as in the first recipe. Blank: take extracted_v3 (null or missing counts as blank); delete all whitespace and every character in the set $ * : . , and the substrings '\[', '\]', '\(', '\)', '\boxed{}', '{}'; the row is blank if nothing remains. Statistic = blank layout rows / layout rows, pooled over the 8 files. If there are fewer than 10 layout rows, the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: measured below 0.40, or fewer than 10 layout rows

predictions.experiment: Where the effect should vanish: blank v3 extractions among finished answers of the hybrid Think-SFT + 2(RL - base) minus the same share for Think-SFT itself, hard328. The mechanism says the RL delta replaces the teacher ending with a boxed line, so the hybrid's blank share falls below Think-SFT's. A reader who treats the hybrid's gain as pure finishing expects no change in the blank share of finished answers.
predictions.recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/transplant/hard328-01/rows.jsonl. Arm H = rows with arm == 'sft1_rl20' (both samples); arm T = rows with arm == 'think' (the 4 reference samples). Finished = cap_hit not true. Blank is defined on extracted_v3 exactly as in the third recipe (null or missing counts as blank). Statistic = (blank finished H rows / finished H rows) - (blank finished T rows / finished T rows). Cap hits are excluded; every row of the arm is used, with no deduplication.
predictions.unit: difference of fractions of finished answers

predictions.experiment: GPU: Think-SFT + 2 x (RL-Math - base), cue, MATH-500 n 500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, one sample, seeds 181000000 + problem_index, full text kept. Count the finished, v3-wrong rows whose candidate after the last 'Answer:' agrees with gold (first recipe's procedure). Think-SFT gives about 4 per sample (result-818c20).

forecasts.reason: Think-SFT single 459.5 + ~4 from the boxed ending ending the v3 layout miss + ~4 reliability from the RL delta; a=2 at the MATH-500 plateau, about like a=1's 467.
Singles 234/229 (mean 231.5), each with ~2 grading points recovered; a vote adds less than Think-SFT's +32 because the hybrid finishes (54 cap hits) at lower precision, so about +18.
Think-SFT 60.0 per sample; the hybrid's hard328 relative gain (+11 %) plus ~0.5 from grading on 136.
Single ~66 plus a vote gain of about +7 (between RL's +6.5 and Think-SFT's larger abstention-driven gain).
Think-SFT vote 241 at 16k; at 32k many of its 29 % cap hits finish with ~68 % precision on long answers; the v3 layout loss (~2 per sample) persists because the teacher ending is unchanged.
Same samples cut at 16,384 tokens reproduce the stored 16k vote (241) up to seed noise; layout loss unchanged.
Think-SFT 60.0 per sample on fresh2026, vote adds about +8 as on hard328 scaled, 32k adds ~3 from finished long answers; layout loss ~0.5 stays.
Same samples scored at 16k: the fresh vote without the long-answer finishes.

no_intervention: The mechanism concerns Think-SFT's teacher answer layout under grader v3, and the RL delta that removes it. The untrained base already writes its value on the same line as 'Answer:' or in a box, which v3 reads (result-0018d3: 0 wrong accepted, misses are other forms), so no prompt, sampling, decoding or selection change to the base follows from it.
